name: Aflac
description: Aflac sells supplemental insurance that pays cash benefits directly to the policyholder for things like a cancer diagnosis, a hospital stay or an accident, on top of regular health cover. Aflac Japan is the larger business (53% of 2025 adjusted revenues, 76% of assets) and Japan's largest seller of cancer and medical policies; Aflac U.S. sells mainly through employers at work (accident, disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, dental/vision, life). Money comes from premiums collected over many years on policies that rarely lapse, with profit equal to premiums less benefits and expenses plus investment income on a large bond portfolio, much of it in Japan Government Bonds and yen assets. It buys back stock heavily.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6321 (Accident & Health Insurance). Over half of revenue and 76% of assets are in Japan and denominated in yen, so US-listed Aflac is largely a Japanese cancer and medical insurer with a US worksite supplemental arm.

employees.note: Aflac Japan 6,804; Aflac U.S. 5,117; corporate and other 795 (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Aflac Japan
businessLines.how: Policyholders pay level premiums monthly or annually, often for life, for fixed cash benefits on diagnosis or hospital stays; Aflac keeps premiums less benefits (benefit ratio guided 60% to 63% for 2026) and expenses, plus yen and dollar bond income. Profit in US dollars moves with the yen (average 149.32 per dollar in 2025).
businessLines.description: Third-sector (cancer, medical, nursing care) insurance plus WAYS and child endowment; sold through about 6,300 agencies (112,000 associates), Dai-ichi Life (about 37,000 reps) and 358 banks.

businessLines.name: Aflac U.S.
businessLines.how: Employees choose and pay for optional policies through payroll deduction at their employer, and employers buy group versions; Aflac earns premium less claims and expenses, and new sales spike in Q4 with open enrollment.
businessLines.description: Worksite and group supplemental insurance: accident, disability, critical care (cancer, critical illness, ICU), hospital indemnity, dental/vision, life; about 5,300 producing agents and brokers.

businessLines.name: Corporate and other
businessLines.description: Parent-company interest expense, investment activity and small other businesses.
